Follow-up to the third 100-PR round (whole-head supplier review open for the four packages). Head is now 5bc0dbb0.

1. Rebased on main 0b1cccf8: the branch differs from main in exactly the four packages. Predecessor blobs are main's, including research/gauge44-slots-t16 at its reviewed head (κ 0.001672188119205421); the README of the head package records this and the selected #1094 (0.001672660197076918), against which research/gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow is +0.1601%.

2. Whole-head driver: `python3 -B research/gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow/verify_chain.py --main . --work /tmp/wholehead1175` (cold, ~40 min; or `--baseline1042 DIR` on a completed scripts/verify_frontier1042.py replay). It rebuilds the k8 chain with research/gauge44-leaver8's scripts and the vendored PR635 supplier, runs the four packages' own verifiers one on the other (arcflow → unpromo → deepen; t16 on arcflow's locals), the three standard-library recounts, the four price receipts (byte-identical to the committed ones), and `wholehead/check_independent.py`, which applies Josie Elliston's owner/event-window audit (research/t16-owner-audit-seed67: R1–R7, X1, X2, controls) and Sagar Thakrar's pricing (research/pending-claims-independent-pricing) unchanged to every map.

3. Receipt of the cold run: `wholehead/RESULT.json` — 20 stages with script/log SHA256, 594 artifact digests, the rebuilt native provider identities of the three words (c2b29430…, 4ffb07de…, 6ace902a…) against each PLAN's provider_registry, owner inventories (34,560 roles/72 calls per T8 map; 69,120/144 for T16; idle {1:1214,2:1,32:1,48:2443}, {1:72,2:17,3:2,32:1,48:2442}, {48:2460}, {1:2430,2:1,16:1,48:4887}) and the exact κ of each package. On the deepened map the auditor's prefix_gap control has no instance (no partially filled bin), which the receipt records.

The three earlier packages' blobs are unchanged from the reviewed head.

Follow-up (October 15): packing caps and realised fractions, in the census field names. Head is now 979ea2d4.

The queue-ceiling screens (#1264; research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered) read #1175's first package only, hence their "title κ differs from the package" note: the title κ 0.001675338871723469 is research/gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow's recorded κ (RESULT.json, data/SPEC.json, construction/deepen/DEEPEN-PINS-k8.json). Per autoresearch.md, `research/gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow/CLAIM.json` now records all four packages in the census's field names — local_profile_per_call, idle_histogram, global profile, live/calls, word SHA256, exact κ and endpoint — with each word's cap under research/complex-local-word-ceiling and the fraction realised; `wholehead/claim_caps.py --main .` recomputes it (standard library, ~20 s).

| package | word | κ | model cap | realised |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gauge44-slots-arcflow | c2b29430… | 0.001674083482880778 | 0.0016872026 | 0.9922 |
| gauge44-slots-t16-arcflow | c2b29430… | 0.001674087289164567 | 0.0016872026 | 0.9922 |
| gauge44-slots-unpromo-arcflow | 4ffb07de… | 0.001674576537247681 | 0.0016828484 | 0.9951 |
| gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow | 6ace902a… | 0.001675338871723469 | 0.0016832052 | 0.9953 |

On the deepened word the map attains the stock-feasible optimum (idle {48:2460}: every idle unit in a rank-48 child, the largest idle bin of the retained template); its residual 0.47% to the model cap is the rank-48/rank-51 idealisation, not unrealised packing. The slot word has the higher model cap but realises less of it because the cap ignores widths (its 240 width-9 helpers lack partners) — an instance of the census's own caution that caps alone do not order attainable optima. Within this model nothing further is available on these words.

wholehead/RESULT.json, STAGES.json and INDEPENDENT.json were regenerated by a fresh cold whole-head run on the final package state (20 stages, all four κ reproduced).

Fifth package (head d3a5d692): research/gauge44-slots-balance-arcflow, κ = 0.001675784247432857 — fourteen restored entrances and ten deepened ends on the slot word c2b29430…, perfectly packed (idle {48:2463}).

Pricing the frame moves against perfect packing shows research/gauge44-slots-deepen-arcflow over-converted: a restored entrance (width 4→5) costs 0.0057 moment units per helper and call and removes one rank-1 remainder worth 0.0066, so once the packing is perfect every further restoration is a loss. A joint integer programme over conversion counts and time-free bin patterns gives fourteen restorations and ten deepenings; the exact frame re-optimisation prices the two entrances left promoted cheapest when they are two of {603, 605, 606, 607} (603 and 605 in the recipe). Details and the comparison table in the README.

+0.0266% over the deepened package, +0.1868% over the selected #1094, 0.0015% below the census's top claims (#1239/#1218/#1193). Cap under research/complex-local-word-ceiling 0.0016836644, realised 0.99532, stock-feasible optimum attained; CLAIM.json covers all five packages.

Verification: construction/balance/verify_balance.py on a completed research/gauge44-slots-arcflow replay (recipe, four rejected mutants, native locals, independent audit, strict replay); verify_chain.py now replays all five packages from one cold k8 reconstruction (wholehead/RESULT.json: 25 stages, 695 artifact digests, both independent auditors on every map). Nothing else in the branch changed; the four earlier packages are as reviewed.

Maintainer review of `99cb4fbf2b55a5e8265e066a1e4793d92f9b5077`: the integer elimination preserves rational row equivalence, and both normal/optimized production checks pass on our macOS replay. Two integration issues remain:

1. `check_temp_corruption_rejection()` catches its own `require(foil_out != honest_out, ...)`. If the checker succeeds with identical output, that assertion is caught and reported as `rejected=True, mode=subprocess_failure`. I reproduced this by substituting `run_xcheck=lambda script: b'identical successful receipt'`; the returned detail is literally `foil accepted with identical complete stdout`. Keep the successful-output comparison outside the subprocess-failure handler and add a control that requires this scenario to fail.
2. Existing registered historical replay `research/r420-rref-performance/adapter.py:bind_sources()` still unconditionally validates the original xcheck digest and now fails at import. Other live consumers also pin it. Demoting the triple-bases input to provenance does not repair executable consumers or preserve their historical A/B comparison. Please retain an immutable baseline for historical replays, route their actual executed inputs to it (or provide an explicitly source-bound historical replay mechanism), and verify affected registered commands without weakening pins. Do not just relabel a consumed input as provenance.

This is a production-integration hold, not a rejection of the speedup or its author benchmark. Baseline output equality and original attribution are valuable; they need to survive together with existing reproduction commands. Our supplemental evidence is retained in the efficient1300 audit as `combined-r420-regression.json` (published with the next review checkpoint).

Maintainer review of `feb0b96b5c471be0a8c72e6ecb8f9e1f74b48991`: the cache correctly keys geometry and reruns `full()`/`interface()` on a fresh Word; the normal production receipt comparison passes. There is an integration regression to address before merging.

`research/r420-rref-performance/adapter.py:bind_sources()` validates every original execution input at import, including `research/e8-bit-r420/code/mutants.py`. Its manifest still requires `e2fd3429...`, while this PR installs `bc6b0106...`, so this previously retained historical replay fails immediately. Updating/demoting the geometry-cache package's pin alone does not cover this consumer, and a consumed baseline must not simply become unbound provenance.

Please preserve the original baseline bytes for historical A/B replays, route their executable inputs to those immutable copies (or an explicit pinned historical replay), inventory other executable consumers, and demonstrate affected registered replays still work. Coordinate with #2263 because both modify the same production manifest and R420 historical inputs. The production logic itself looks promising; this hold concerns reproducibility and integration, not the claimed mathematical result or host-specific benchmark ratio.

Supplemental exact-head pin evidence will be in `research/community-efficient1300-audit/combined-r420-regression.json` at the next checkpoint.

Maintainer review of `68a7161a610f175dc8e7b22f95acd033191450d9`: the gate-table rewrite has a plausible exact recurrence, and the recorded normal/optimized package replays pass. Before production integration, please fix the runtime source-binding regression.

`clifford-reciprocal-basis-obstruction/dense.py:native_module()` still imports `V.ROOT / V.KERNEL`, but this PR removes that actual runtime dependency from `INPUTS`, `VERIFY.json` and `CERTIFICATE.json`, marking it as provenance. It also changes the former kernel-drift negative control to mutate `selector-batching/README.md` instead. I reproduced that appending bytes to the executed Clifford oracle is now accepted by `check_sources()` with an unchanged reported source inventory.

A consumed oracle is an input, not historical provenance. Please preserve a pinned original runtime baseline for the historical replay, or explicitly migrate the replay to a pinned optimized oracle with complete regenerated evidence and the original drift-control coverage. Keep immutable evidence intact and audit the same issue in `cold-wrapper-amplitude-audit`, whose executed-source pin is also removed. Include a control proving kernel source drift and missing kernel inventory are rejected; do not substitute a README mutation for that coverage.

This is a reproducibility/integration hold, not a rejection of the speedup. Exact evidence is retained in the efficient1300 audit as `combined-2329-source-control.py/.json`, to be published with this checkpoint.

**Correction (author).** The "≈ 0.0017259" estimate in this PR is wrong, and so are the model prices F/C/C8 (0.0017255 / 0.0017127 / 0.0017141). None of them is attainable on the PR2269 T74 template with unsplit helpers. The width-blind R = 48 cap here (0.0017480) is still a valid upper bound, but a loose one.

- An actual legal 400-helper owner fill of these words reaches b = 0.00168654323627, which is 0.57% **below** #2269.
- An exact width-aware LP-dual certificate shows that **every** legal whole-helper fill has b < 0.0016867. The width-9 low lenders fragment the rank-16/32 bins, which costs more than the 121 freed rank units.
- The "+5 high" variant gives exactly zero gain.

Details, fill, checks and certificate: #2387. #2360 (Jeremy Diviney) independently certifies b < 0.0016870. The local construction in this PR is unaffected; it should be read as a no-gain inventory for this template.

Maintainer review at `b5c3b567f13b18881161cf6c445e4ef251870558`: the `r439-abc-hosted-invoice` manifest change needs revision before integration.

`audit_hosted_k.py` is still a live computational input, not just provenance. `verify.py` invokes `e8-bit-p111-tuned/code/adapt9p.py` with the vendored code directory; that adapter reads `code/audit_hosted_k.py` to produce the hosted auditor executed later. I replayed the exact parent adapter and instrumented port adapter at this head. The read inventory contains:

```
research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/vendor/pr510/e8-r480-nine-stage/vendor/e8-r715-eleven-stage-whole/code/audit_hosted_k.py
```

It is absent from the declared input set after this PR demotes it. Consequently the full verifier's `consumed <= set(inputs)` gate will reject it even if the preceding native stages succeed. This is an actual adapter replay, not a full native-pipeline replay or a claim that the digest optimization is mathematically incorrect.

Please retain a live binding for the auditor actually consumed: either preserve a pinned historical baseline through the adapter chain, or explicitly bind and replay the updated implementation with the affected complete receipts and rejection controls. Do not remove the consumed-input coverage gate. The other manifest changes and production equivalence still need their complete review.

Maintainer review at `3bc76f12b29732e901f13b19d341253379f04cb1`: the integer-row implementation and historical-baseline approach are promising, but the downstream migration is incomplete.

1. Two registered checks (`complex-signed-prefix-audit` and `selected1094-wire-prefix-audit`) change their source key without updating `EXPECTED.json`. `complex-stage-diagonal-normalization-seed24/CERTIFICATE.json` has the same issue in `source_hashes`. I reproduced the first receipt mismatch, made local repairs that only rename the key to the byte-identical `complex-sw4-frame8` checker, and replayed the affected checks. The diagonal certificate and historical opt-in integer checker both pass after that correction. These local corrections do not change mathematical fields and will be retained in the review evidence.

2. Other live-bound consumers still use the replaced k492 path. In particular, I executed `complex-ck-target-forest/verify.py:check_sources` at this head: it rejects `source pin: research/complex-k492-owner-repair/code/hpe_audit_local.py`. Restoring only the original checker bytes makes that complete source check pass. This is a regression introduced by the production rewrite, not an already-stale selected-result pointer. `replica-prefix-audit` and `supplier-circuit-consolidation` also have live source-check loops over manifests containing this path, and the JP8 native replay helpers still execute it.

Please complete the consumer inventory and preserve authenticated historical execution for those consumers as well, using the retained byte-identical checker/baseline where appropriate. Update each affected source-key receipt through its generator and retain its semantic fields and rejection coverage. A source-hash demotion alone is not sufficient for executable dependencies.

The selected frontier remains unchanged. This review does not dispute the scalar-row equivalence or independently certify the reported host-specific speedup; it is holding production integration until downstream replay compatibility is complete.

Independent check in #2442: your window-free-optimality claim holds, and more strongly. Over the bin-pattern integer relaxation of all legal whole-helper fills of #2322's words, your idle multiset is the unique optimum within 1e-12, and every fill has b ≤ your κ + 1e-15. The check uses an exact rational dual with 800-bit enclosures and exact enumeration. An adversarial reviewer also ran a Gomory group-relaxation check and local search, and could not refute it.

Maintainer integration review at `462593231536f771050da8f44390b3e4eba95783`: the remaining downstream pin migration needs to include at least two more consumers before this production rewrite can land.

I executed `research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639/verify.py:check_pins` against its complete pinned inputs. It passes with the original PR968 source. Replacing only `research/complex-frame-pair-decoders/verify.py` with this PR's production bytes fails with:

```
ValueError: working input SHA drift: research/complex-frame-pair-decoders/verify.py
```

That consumer is not changed in this PR. The newly integrated `research/cycle47-shared-frame-correction` also imports the same model at runtime and lists the original bytes as a live input in SOURCES.json / VERIFY.json. This second dependency arrived after your base, so please include it when refreshing the integration.

Please preserve the historical model for these consumers (or explicitly update their live binding and replay the affected checks), keeping their expected receipt/source metadata consistent. Merely demoting a runtime dependency to provenance would not address reproducibility. A complete manifest-and-loader scan should catch any further consumers.

This is an integration hold, not a rejection of the neighborhood-mask optimization or its numerical results. The optimization's full review remains pending. Exact reproduction evidence will be retained in the efficient1300 batch audit; themilkman216, woklerx and your production-wiring contribution remain credited.
